description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy performance of six different methods across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis represents the "Co-occurrence Number" on a logarithmic scale, with labeled ticks at 0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis represents "ACC (%)" on a linear scale, ranging from 60 to just above 80, with tick marks at intervals of 5 units. The "Base" method is represented by a solid black line with circle markers, starting at an accuracy of approximately 61% at the lowest co-occurrence number (around 3) and steadily increasing to roughly 67% at the highest co-occurrence number (around 3000). The "FT" method is shown as a solid blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, beginning at about 62.5% and rising to approximately 68% at the end of the x-axis. The "IKE" method, depicted by a solid red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, starts at roughly 64.5% and increases to about 70%. The "MEND" method is indicated by a solid brown line with diamond markers, starting at approximately 66%, rising to about 73.5% at a co-occurrence number of 300, and ending at roughly 74%. The "MEMIT" method is represented by a solid purple line with pentagon markers, beginning at about 66.5% and increasing to approximately 72.5% at the highest x-axis value. Finally, the "ROME" method is shown as a solid green line with square markers, starting at approximately 72.5%, increasing to about 77.5% at a co-occurrence number of 300, and remaining steady at 77.5% through the end of the x-axis.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) performance of six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME) on Llama2 across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis represents 'Co-occurrence Number' on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10^1 to 10^3, while the y-axis shows 'ACC (%)' on a linear scale from 60% to 80%. ROME consistently outperforms all other methods, achieving an accuracy of approximately 85% at the highest co-occurrence number. MEMIT and MEND exhibit similar trends, with MEMIT slightly surpassing MEND at lower co-occurrence numbers but falling behind at higher values. FT demonstrates the steepest growth rate, increasing by nearly 10% across the range, while Base remains relatively stable, showing minimal improvement. IKE starts with the highest initial accuracy but stabilizes at around 70%, falling behind MEMIT and MEND at higher co-occurrence numbers.
